items.requirement: P1 · Decide: Define the credential’s promise.** State which 5.0 tasks a graduate can supervise independently, what agent assistance is allowed and what the credential does not establish. Publish the same promise in the course introduction and certificate description. Accepted at checkpoint 206: the pinned draft contract drives the learner introduction and future immutable issuance description/PDF; actual release and live competence verification remain gated.

P1 · Improve: Map outcomes to evidence.** Maintain an outcome matrix linking each required skill to its lesson, practice task, assessment, passing evidence and rubric version. Every required outcome has an assessed home; repeated coverage has a clear purpose. Accepted at checkpoint 209: validated 33-row contract-derived matrix, separate passing criteria for shared lessons/evidence, all-course saved-receipt mapping and CI output. Live assessment validity remains a separate gate.

P1 · Decide: Set progression and remediation policy.** Define prerequisites, optional enrichment, retries, critical errors, star upgrades and accommodations. Chat, panel, API and administrator behavior must implement the same policy. Accepted at checkpoint 293: shared pinned policy, automatic remediation, unchanged assessment criteria for presentation options, supported capability alternatives, and consistent chat/panel/API/admin delivery. Actual release, live calibration and complete assistive-technology observation remain separate gates.

P1 · Improve: Establish the authoritative course manifest.** Derive module order, stable IDs, lesson counts, objectives, XP, prerequisites, required checks and learner-facing criteria from one published definition. Remove independently maintained constants where they can drift.

P1 · Improve: Separate competency from participation.** Label reflections, reading progress and practice as such. Define which evidence earns assessed credit; a submitted reflection or high XP alone cannot imply demonstrated operational competence. Accepted at checkpoint 212: practice/reflection/reading labels and pinned policy distinguish participation; real saved-evidence checks reject missing or failed outcomes despite high XP. Live grading validity remains open.

P2 · Verify: Inventory all course entry and support surfaces.** Cover chat home, action links, learning panel, direct URLs, certificate, help, notifications, email and administrator views. Record which manifest/version each reads and eliminate contradictory descriptions.

P0 · Fix: Repair the progress response contract.** Remove the obsolete `streak_days` dependency or replace it with the intended supported field. The real progress serializer feeding the real chat tool must handle both new and legacy records without an exception.

P1 · Improve: Validate course tool payloads.** Give progress, module, lesson, provisioning, checking, completion and reflection results explicit schemas. Missing or malformed required fields must produce actionable errors rather than blank cards or invented default success.

P1 · Verify: Make course entry reliable.** Exercise Start, Continue and the explicit certification action link with new, active and certified enrollments. Each reaches the intended course/version and next valid action, with no generic chat fallback presented as a course response.

P1 · Fix: Distinguish live results from replay.** Replace result-on-mount inference with explicit live/history provenance. A tool call and result delivered together still refresh progress; loading historical messages cannot award credit or trigger write side effects.

P1 · Verify: Synchronize every relevant write.** Lab provisioning, saved reflections, completion, star upgrades and migration update chat, panel, home CTA and badge from the same enrollment state. Test buffered and incremental responses.

P1 · Improve: Handle refresh failures visibly.** A completed write followed by a failed progress read must say progress is awaiting refresh and offer retry. Preserve the successful operation and prevent the learner from repeating it to repair a display issue.

P1 · Improve: Prevent duplicate submissions.** Disable or deduplicate pending lesson/assessment/completion actions and support server idempotency. Double-clicks, Enter plus click, retries and two tabs cannot create duplicate attempts or XP awards.

P1 · Improve: Detect obsolete card actions.** Bind buttons to enrollment, module and relevant revision. Old conversation cards must not silently submit work to a new course version or grade an obsolete artifact; offer a current-course action when necessary. Accepted at checkpoint 214: complete course identity and module guards disable obsolete card actions; server stale-write and changed-answer checks retain original evidence/credit. Historical reading and certificate access remain available.

P1 · Verify: Recover after interruption.** Refreshing, reconnecting or reopening chat during provisioning, assessment save or completion reconciles actual server state and presents the next safe action. Partial output is not treated as proof that a write succeeded. Accepted at checkpoint 280: exact saved request/answer/evidence recovery, truthful sample status, fenced late callbacks, read-only receipt checks and explicit completion resumption are verified through current component checks plus retained browser/HTTP/disposable-MongoDB evidence. Live provider behavior, deployed worker rollout and external vector/KB side effects remain separate gates.

P1 · Fix: Enforce the progression policy consistently.** Remove the temporary prerequisite bypass and apply the decided rules at the service boundary. Any permitted admin override must be explicit, scoped and recorded; a prompt cannot bypass a required prerequisite. Accepted at checkpoint 233: legacy any-order access matches its preserved rubric, pinned requirements remain enforced, missing definitions cannot use fallback access, and staff changes are scoped and recorded at checkpoint 231. No assessed requirements were weakened.

P1 · Verify: Explain unavailable agent capabilities.** Missing team membership, unavailable model/tools, permission denial or unsupported capabilities must produce a clear path forward. Provide the supported panel/editor route where available without suggesting the chat action succeeded.

P2 · Improve: Make long-running course actions understandable.** Show actual preparation, processing, checking and completion states. Explain the effect of cancel/retry and preserve completed work; do not display fabricated progress, timing or success. Accepted at checkpoint 289: actual action-state labels, closure/retry guidance and retained-work boundaries are verified across preparation, execution, grading, completion and course choices. No provider cancellation or timing guarantee is implied.

P1 · Fix: Repair the mobile lesson header.** Stack or wrap title and lesson metadata so the title remains readable at 320px and 390px. No single-letter columns, overlapping labels or clipped module names may remain.

P1 · Improve: Restore useful mobile reading width.** Remove unnecessary nested indentation and adapt existing navigation/pane controls without losing file-and-tool context. The lesson should use available width and require only normal vertical reading.

P1 · Fix: Eliminate nested clipping.** Inspect actual card, transcript and pane bounds as well as page width. Long titles, criteria, errors, field names and buttons must remain visible or deliberately scrollable within a named region.

P2 · Improve: Set course typography deliberately.** Use readable body text, clear title/section hierarchy, comfortable line length and spacing. Dense metadata must not compete with the lesson; verify real fonts and enlarged text rather than relying on screenshots at reduced scale.

P1 · Fix: Render authored Markdown consistently.** Safely render supported overview and instruction formatting so raw `**` markers disappear. Lists, links and emphasis must preserve meaning without enabling unsafe markup.
P2 · Fix: Show numbered procedure steps.** Ordered lab instructions must display readable step numbers and wrap cleanly. Distinguish instructions, expected results and optional enrichment visually.

P2 · Improve: Clarify the primary action.** For each state, prioritize the appropriate action: start/resume lesson, practice, verify, remediate or complete. Avoid presenting completion as equivalent to preparation before the learner has done the required work.

P2 · Improve: Reduce long-card overload.** Separate lesson introduction, lab steps, expected fields and optional star criteria with meaningful disclosure where useful. Essential requirements and current next actions must remain discoverable without hiding failures. Accepted at checkpoint 215: early module actions, keyboard instruction/field disclosure and always-visible required outcomes or legacy passing criteria; all eleven chat-to-panel entries verified at narrow/desktop/native zoom.

P1 · Verify: Keep actions reachable on short screens.** Check top and bottom states with the composer, on-screen keyboard and sticky navigation present. The learner can reach and activate every required control without content being permanently covered.

P2 · Verify: Preserve desktop split-view composition.** Inspect teaching beside files, source evidence, extraction and workflow editors at realistic pane widths. Opening or closing the course must preserve document selection, draft changes and current work.

P2 · Improve: Use coherent status and completion visuals.** Loading, saved, completed, failed, advisory and certified states must look distinct and match their meanings. Avoid relying on decorative stars or tool status to communicate learner completion.

P2 · Verify: Check theme and content extremes.** Exercise supported theme/accent settings, long learner names, long module titles, large XP values, URLs, tables and all supported lesson content types. Token choices must preserve readable contrast and hierarchy.

P1 · Fix: Resolve measured contrast failures.** Replace weak metadata and success colors using shared semantic tokens. Recheck progress, lesson, check, completion and certificate states; close the recorded axe findings without removing meaningful information.

P1 · Improve: Expose course structure semantically.** Use meaningful headings and named progress information. Screen-reader users can identify the module, lesson position, required checks, current result and next action without interpreting layout alone.

P1 · Verify: Complete the course controls with a keyboard.** Exercise cards, disclosures, answer choices, source links, editor handoffs, validation, recovery and certificate access. Focus order follows reading order and never traps users in a nonmodal pane.

P1 · Verify: Maintain visible focus.** All interactive course elements show clear focus under supported themes and after scrolling. Focus is not obscured by the composer, sticky headers, dialogs or split panes.

P1 · Verify: Announce meaningful changes.** A screen reader receives saved answers, grading results, failures and awarded credit without the entire streaming transcript being repeatedly announced. Verify with actual assistive technology, not only an accessibility-tree dump.

P1 · Verify: Manage modal and handoff focus.** Verification dialogs and celebrations contain focus appropriately; Escape closes the intended layer and restores a useful target. Nonmodal course panels remain usable alongside the workspace. Accepted at checkpoint 329: fullscreen and source-preview dialogs, tier/course celebrations and editor handoffs have actual keyboard containment/exit/return evidence; docked panels permit workspace focus. Current panel checks and 71 focused cases pass. This does not substitute for actual screen-reader announcements or mobile OS keyboard verification.

P1 · Improve: Make assessment controls accessible.** Associate questions, answer groups, instructions and errors; expose selected and required states. A learner can correct an answer and understand grading feedback without color or pointer input.

P2 · Improve: Provide alternatives for diagrams and stars.** Diagrams need equivalent explanatory text; star counts, status icons and progress changes need meaningful accessible labels where they carry information. Hide purely decorative icons from the reading order.

P1 · Verify: Support actual enlargement.** Check actual 200% browser zoom, enlarged text and narrow-screen reflow. Device pixel ratio alone is insufficient; lesson headings, answer groups and primary actions must remain usable.

P2 · Verify: Support touch and reduced motion.** Controls must have usable target size/spacing and work without hover. Reduced-motion settings preserve status, reading position and completion feedback without essential animated-only cues.

P1 · Improve: Resume by stable lesson identity.** Persist a server-side enrollment cursor using lesson IDs, not array indexes. Chat and panel resume the same lesson across reloads, browsers and devices, with an explicit reset or restart action when appropriate.

P1 · Improve: Distinguish viewed from completed learning.** Store and label reading position, knowledge-check attempts, practice and assessed credit separately. Opening a lesson must not silently certify understanding or satisfy an assessed outcome. Accepted at checkpoint 234: browser-local formative attempt history is scoped to the learner/course/lesson revision and explicitly separate from the saved reading cursor, reflections and server-assessed credit; no practice interaction writes course progress.

P2 · Improve: Provide dependable lesson navigation.** Support next, previous, lesson list and return to current lesson with stable IDs. Navigation must not depend on the LLM inferring a title or correct numeric offset.

P1 · Fix: Render authored knowledge checks directly.** Present questions, choices, feedback and retry deterministically in chat and panel. The agent may explain feedback but must not be the only mechanism that exposes a required check.

P2 · Fix: Restore instructional diagrams in chat.** Preserve supported diagram identity/content through the export/tool contract and render the same teaching concept in both surfaces. A text equivalent remains available at narrow widths and to assistive technology.

P1 · Fix: Make lab setup a real course action.** Replace references to nonexistent buttons with an actual provisioning control and accurate copy. Show preparing, processing, ready and failed states; identify the resulting lab folder/documents and the next step. Accepted at checkpoint 239: explicit setup plus authenticated assigned-document status separates preparation, processing, text readiness, failure and unavailable state; folder/files, safe recovery and keyboard focus are verified through HTTP persistence and narrow/desktop/native-zoom views. External ingestion and concurrent creation remain separate gates.

P1 · Improve: Preserve learner-authored answers.** Save reflective answers and drafts at appropriate checkpoints, show saved state, and preserve them through errors or session expiry. The agent must not invent or silently replace the learner’s responses. Accepted at checkpoint 235: authenticated learner/course-bound reflection drafts survive remounts, failed saves and simulated expiry, confirmed original answers win over local drafts, and explicit V5 decisions retain their original saved evidence. Browser-tab drafts are labeled separately from course saves.

P2 · Improve: Make editor handoffs explicit.** Explain why a precision editor is needed, open the correct artifact, preserve chat/lesson position and provide a return-to-course action. Completion evidence must still recognize the same attempt. Accepted at checkpoint 248: checkpoints 242–247 verify exact editor/sample navigation and retained course/chat; connected real-API instruction repair, recapture and retest preparation preserve field identity, required titles, original failed evidence and unchanged expectations. Chrome, WebKit and native zoom pass; no repair automatically runs, grades or awards credit.

P1 · Improve: Explain failed grading and remediation.** Show the failed requirement, relevant evidence and a concrete repair/recheck action. Preserve successful checks and make retry limits or review routes visible where the course policy requires them. Accepted at checkpoint 285: original criteria/evidence/repair guidance, explicit scenario/work return actions, preserved prior checks, scoped rechecks and technical retry lineage are verified through current frontend, integrity and disposable-persistence checks plus retained browser evidence. Live grading calibration and learner comprehension remain separate gates.

P2 · Fix: Complete the graduation journey.** Show actual course/version, earned credit, certificate access and what to do next in chat and panel. Add a usable chat certificate action and remove hardcoded XP totals or module counts.

P1 · Improve: Make agent supervision a course-wide skill.** Thread scope selection, proposal review, source checking, correction, recovery and delivery through the modules. Add assessed outcomes rather than merely rewriting editor steps as chat prompts.

P1 · Fix: Correct quality claims everywhere.** Explain that Unscored is possible, template scores describe tested examples and additional test cases may expose failures. Remove guarantees that every result has a score or more verification necessarily increases it. Accepted at checkpoints 303/305: working and V5 teaching correct these claims; the same dated guidance supplements ten affected frozen lessons in the panel and tutor payload and also appears on old-format chat cards. Exact text matches support unversioned cards without inventing their historical course. Original lesson bytes, assessment requirements and earned credit remain preserved.

P1 · Fix: Correct arithmetic guidance.** Clearly distinguish LLM analysis from deterministic calculation. The budget exercise must verify arithmetic through a supported calculation method or explicit human calculation; Deep Analysis alone is not proof that totals are correct. Accepted at checkpoints 291/292/307: the bounded budget exercise checks recorded calculations against source inputs; corrected working and V5 teaching separate model interpretation from independently checked arithmetic. A dated notice corrects six affected historical lessons in panel and old chat cards without rewriting their original requirements or credit.

P1 · Improve: Teach source and scope distinctions.** Explain selected files, project knowledge, attached knowledge bases and public web information using the actual product behavior. Include the consequences of choosing the wrong team, project or document. Accepted at checkpoint 309: Foundations distinguishes selected document context, project knowledge override, separately attached knowledge-base retrieval and configured public web lookup. It explains bounded/missing source coverage, readiness and search failure, workspace-wide tool limits and concrete wrong-scope corrections.

P1 · Improve: Teach approval decisions.** Include approve, reject and revise examples with actual action targets and consequences. State which tools preview changes and which do not; do not generalize beyond implemented behavior. Accepted at checkpoint 308: concrete paused-run approval/rejection and pre-run scope revision examples explain targets, permissions, consequences, saved outcomes, cancellation limits and the differing preview behavior of workflow and extraction actions.

P1 · Improve: Teach recovery from partial work.** Cover a failed tool, incomplete batch, interrupted chat and expired context. Show how to inspect persisted outcomes before retrying and explain that canceling a response does not necessarily undo completed actions. Accepted at checkpoint 310: Foundations provides controlled failed-tool, interrupted-chat, lost/expired-context and incomplete-batch recovery examples, aligned with saved-result inspection and the existing connected/batch recovery lessons. Generic retry is distinguished from checking status; completed work and unresolved outcomes remain explicit.

P1 · Improve: Teach data and instruction boundaries.** Include a source document containing misleading instructions and a proposal to send data outside the intended scope. Learners must recognize that document text cannot authorize actions or override their task. Accepted at checkpoint 311: a complete fictional source is packaged and shown inline with its misleading instruction, an explicitly incorrect external-send proposal, a scoped correction and the expected internal result. The unchanged required recognition case rejects treating source text as authorization.

P2 · Fix: Align copy with current controls and counts.** Reconcile lesson counts, node names, star descriptions, available actions and realistic time estimates. Remove unexplained internal tool names and unsupported time-saving claims from learner copy. Accepted at checkpoint 328: source-reviewed teaching, lab/module/exercise guidance, dated preserved-course corrections and formative feedback now match current supported controls and disclose original rubric limits. Tier completion no longer claims an unearned course credential. This accepts copy accuracy; legacy rubric equivalence and live V5 assessment remain separate gates.

P1 · Improve: Build representative practice and failure cases.** Include correct, ambiguous, missing, scanned and incorrect results with documented expected evidence. Every intentionally wrong example is clearly controlled and has a valid recovery path.

P2 · Verify: Keep panel and chat teaching in sync.** Validate the authored lessons, exported data, diagrams, checks, reflection questions and exercises against the same manifest in CI. A stale generated export must fail the publication check. Accepted at checkpoint 216: exact source/export verification and deliberate stale-export/authoring refusal checks run in the existing CI paths; immutable package hashes bind exercises and delivery shares reflection definitions.

P1 · Fix: Rewrite the agentic introduction accurately.** Demonstrate what chat can read, propose and execute, with real limits on quality scores, source grounding and agent judgment. Remove claims contradicted by the later QA lessons. Accepted at checkpoint 296: revised introduction matches current operation-specific preview/creation/execution behavior, source-grounding and Unscored/quality limits; all nine lesson drafts have prior course coverage and the corrected lessons have current narrow/desktop/native-zoom checks. Live tutoring and beginner/practical validation remain separate gates.

P1 · Improve: Add a first scoped chat exercise.** The learner selects the intended source, asks a bounded question and opens its supporting passage. Successful practice requires noticing when an answer lacks the requested evidence.

P1 · Improve: Assess the basic supervision decisions.** Use short scenarios on unsafe assumptions, a wrong target and an unsupported answer. Record learner choices and remediation; reflective comfort/experience responses remain ungraded reflection. Accepted at checkpoint 277: nine pinned recognition scenarios cover all three basic supervision outcomes; all eighteen wrong choices fail their required outcome, authenticated immutable choices/feedback and correction history are preserved, and explicit read-only recovery is verified. Recognition does not substitute for practical execution, the beginner pilot or the remaining module/release gates.

P2 · Verify: Support the true beginner path.** A new learner can finish with no prior artifacts or technical vocabulary. Both surfaces show the correct lesson count, explain lab versus personal data and resume after interruption.

P1 · Fix: Reconcile the chat and workflow routes.** Teach creation of a reusable extraction from chat and explain when a workflow wrapper is useful. Both supported routes must have accurate instructions and equivalent completion evidence.

P1 · Improve: Inspect the proposed extraction before creation.** Have the learner confirm the sample document, field meanings, artifact name and target scope, and correct a deliberately inappropriate proposed field or target.

P1 · Fix: Grade the actual lab run.** Require the intended extraction revision to run on the assigned NSF sample, and verify required values against the source. Fields or runs on unrelated artifacts cannot satisfy the module.

P2 · Fix: Make star criteria truthful.** Publish exact required and enrichment fields from the rubric, and assess them on the same attempt. Show missing evidence and support field repair followed by re-execution.

P2 · Improve: Teach the choice of working method.** Compare one-off chat, a project, a saved extraction, a workflow and an automation using concrete RA tasks. Explain when an extra saved process adds unnecessary complexity. Accepted at checkpoint 304: the unpublished V5 teaching compares all five methods using RA examples, distinguishes project organization from triggered execution, and explains the cost of unnecessary saved processes. Actual capability/default-state source review, preview integrity and focused narrow/desktop/native-zoom practice evidence support this teaching acceptance; live assessment and learner observation remain separate.

P1 · Improve: Map a process with human decisions.** The learner identifies inputs, repetitive tasks, deterministic calculations, institutional judgment, handoffs and outputs. The agent can suggest a map but the learner must correct an intentional boundary mistake.

P1 · Improve: Assess the process decision.** Require a short rationale for the selected method and human checkpoint, using a rubric for appropriate scope and task fit. Merely entering nonempty reflection answers does not establish this outcome.

P2 · Verify: Connect the map to later work.** Save the learner’s approved process description for Workflow Design, with an option to choose a provided example. Missing personal examples must not block progress or force disclosure of sensitive work.

P2 · Improve: Teach iterative design in chat.** Demonstrate requirements, proposed architecture, refinement and editor inspection. Include a valid short-document design that does not require extraction simply to add steps. Accepted at checkpoint 313: a concrete short-note iteration progresses from bounded requirements through an overbuilt proposal, refinement to supported Prompt/Formatter or single-Prompt work, same-artifact editor inspection and actual-output checks. This accepts teaching, not live design assessment.

P1 · Improve: Require critique of a flawed proposal.** The learner finds a wrong input, unnecessary step, missing human checkpoint or inappropriate output. Record the correction before approving the saved design.

P1 · Improve: Assess architecture against the process goal.** Check input/output compatibility, data flow, justified task types and reviewer needs. Reflection can accompany the design but cannot substitute for the assessed artifact and decisions.

P2 · Verify: Preserve one design across surfaces.** Switching between chat and editor keeps the same artifact/revision and course attempt. The learner can inspect the final design and explain why it fits the intended work.

P1 · Improve: Teach field quality over field quantity.** Cover precise names, optional values, categorical constraints, absence versus hallucination and representative source evidence. Explain which settings can be authored through chat and which need the editor. Accepted at checkpoint 313: existing precise-field/category/absence teaching now identifies the document-discovery creation route’s limits and the editor’s persisted Optional/Allowed values controls. Source semantics and post-repair execution remain explicit; practical field-repair grading is separate.

P1 · Fix: Replace the unrelated-field passing condition.** Required fields must belong to the assigned extraction revision and produce an assessed result on the NIH lab. Fifteen arbitrary fields, an unexecuted template or fields spread across unrelated templates cannot pass.

P1 · Improve: Require correction and guided verification.** Include a wrong budget or investigator value and an absent field. The learner inspects the source, repairs the configuration or expected value appropriately and verifies a new result.

P1 · Fix: Align higher-star checks with their promises.** If categories, optional fields, budget breakdowns or accuracy earn stars, validate those properties explicitly. The summary and individual checks must agree about pass, failure and optional advice.

P2 · Improve: Teach inspection of actual data flow.** Follow the assigned subaward through extraction, reasoning and formatting, opening each step’s input/output. Explain both expected chains and valid alternatives without rewarding gratuitous complexity.

P1 · Improve: Add a failed-step recovery exercise.** A learner identifies the failed stage, preserves successful work and chooses the supported retry/edit route. The exercise must not train users to repeat completed writes indiscriminately.

P1 · Fix: Grade one executed workflow.** Require the necessary task types, compatible connections and a successful assessed run on the assigned input. Step counts or task types aggregated across different workflows cannot satisfy the rubric.

P2 · Fix: Reconcile enrichment criteria.** Resolve the four-versus-five-task-type inconsistency and assess useful complexity and output quality on the same workflow. Every star description must match the published rubric.

P1 · Fix: Replace misleading numerical verification.** Rewrite the Deep Analysis budget example so the arithmetic is independently calculated and checked. Teach what the two LLM passes can contribute without claiming deterministic correctness. Accepted at checkpoint 291: revision-3 worked example independently computes a fictional source discrepancy, distinguishes analysis/synthesis from calculation, and preserves unresolved source meaning. Deterministic arithmetic/source checks veto a synthetic model pass; actual draft release and live calibration remain separate.

P1 · Improve: Teach permissions and capability boundaries.** Explain ordinary versus admin-only nodes, external API/crawler effects and credential handling. Provide an equivalent path that requires neither admin access nor real external secrets. Accepted at checkpoint 292: credential and permission teaching matches the bounded runner, with ordinary one/two-Prompt source review and recorded arithmetic; unsupported nodes and conflicting assignment instructions are rejected. Actual release and live assessment validity remain separate.

P1 · Fix: Require executed advanced and parallel work.** Grade a specific workflow/run where the advanced task and intended parallel tasks have real outputs. Configuration presence alone or unrelated tasks in another workflow cannot pass.

P2 · Improve: Assess tool choice and recovery.** Have the learner choose an appropriate node, justify independence for parallel tasks and handle an unavailable or failed capability. Accept a supported safe alternative when the environment lacks an optional integration.

P2 · Improve: Teach audience and output selection.** Match document, structured export and form output to the recipient’s task. Show the real editor handoff for unsupported chat authoring and return to the same course attempt.

P1 · Fix: Require output from the assessed run.** Tie the output node, executed workflow and downloadable artifact to the same attempt. An output configuration in one workflow and an unrelated executed workflow cannot earn completion.

P1 · Improve: Verify the delivered artifact.** The learner opens the actual file and checks key values, missing information and intended recipients/scope. Test malformed or missing output as a repairable failure, not successful delivery.

P2 · Fix: Verify bundle and enrichment behavior.** Grade the supported multiple-deliverable ZIP path and its actual contents. Remove reliance on unavailable Package Builder behavior; teach what the download contains and how to retrieve it again.

P1 · Improve: Teach the complete quality vocabulary.** Distinguish Unscored, measured quality, stale evidence, active alerts, successful execution and examiner approval. The learner must explain why a strong template score does not certify the current answer. Accepted at checkpoint 312: explicit status definitions and a combined-state example accompany the existing explanation practice and required historical-score recognition case. Author-assigned ratings, configurable age/configuration staleness and acknowledgment without repair are distinguished; practical repair and live calibration remain separate.

P1 · Improve: Require grounded test-case creation.** Have the learner inspect and correct expected values against original sources. The assessment must reject simply accepting a wrong agent-proposed answer as ground truth.

P1 · Fix: Bind checks and validation to one assessment target.** Require the intended test cases and a completed relevant validation run for the assigned template/workflow revision. Counts and run records from unrelated items cannot be combined to pass.

P1 · Improve: Assess response to a failure or regression.** Include a new case that lowers a score or exposes a mismatch. The learner identifies the limitation, makes an appropriate correction and explains the resulting evidence rather than pursuing a higher number blindly.

P1 · Improve: Teach explicit batch scope.** Before execution, the learner reviews the actual documents, template/workflow revision, destination and expected output. Include one wrongly selected file that must be removed.

P1 · Improve: Practice partial failure.** Include an unreadable or failed document. Preserve successful outputs and retry only what needs rerunning using supported controls; make failure versus skipped work clear.

P1 · Fix: Assess the intended successful batch.** Bind grading to assigned input IDs and per-document terminal results. An unrelated historical batch or documents-touched count without adequate result evidence cannot establish the lab outcome.

P2 · Improve: Assess source sampling and consolidated output.** Require spot-checking representative values and identifying an intentionally wrong result before export. Provide sufficient safe sample documents for every published higher-star target.

P1 · Improve: Teach ownership and sharing scope.** Include personal, team, project and broader publication decisions using the actual permission model. The learner must identify an inappropriate sharing target and correct it.

P1 · Improve: Teach ongoing automation effects.** Review a proposed trigger, input filters, action, outputs and enable/disable state. Assess whether the action should be enabled and how it is stopped or inspected, without requiring real external delivery.

P1 · Improve: Assess accountable handoff.** Require a clear artifact description, intended use, limitations and relevant validation evidence. Preserve completion on a valid submission without waiting for examiner availability; examiner acceptance is a separate state.

P1 · Improve: Add the final supervision capstone.** Use an unfamiliar but supported RA task with one flawed proposed action and one bad result. The learner must identify and repair both, verify sources, inspect delivery and justify scope; agent-created artifacts alone cannot pass.

P1 · Improve: Bind an assessment attempt to its evidence.** Record enrollment, module, exercise revision, input documents, artifact revisions and execution IDs. Grading must use that evidence rather than scanning the user’s entire workspace for matching activity. Accepted at checkpoint 227: new competency attempts use authenticated, enrollment/module/package-bound source and artifact snapshots with exact execution/decision references; original selected receipt hashes carry through all eleven modules into credit and credentials. Broader project/team access verification remains C8-GRADE-07.

P1 · Improve: Preserve evidence as assessed.** Store sufficient immutable snapshots or revision references to explain an awarded result after artifact edits/deletion. Later edits must not silently rewrite the evidence behind an issued credential. Accepted at checkpoint 224: all eleven modules retain original selected receipt hashes and assessment evidence through source edits/deletion, answer revisions, technical retries and normal/interrupted full-course issuance; legacy unknown provenance remains explicit.

P1 · Fix: Separate required checks from advice.** Give checks an explicit required/advisory role, compute pass from the required rubric and label the summary accurately. A warning is not a failed mandatory check and “all checks passed” must be literally true. Accepted at checkpoint 225: explicit legacy required/advisory roles preserve the original rubric, typed chat contracts reject contradictory summaries, and chat/panel labels distinguish advice from failure at narrow widths and native 200% zoom.

P1 · Improve: Assess outcomes, not just execution.** A completed job is necessary where required but does not establish correct values, useful output or source verification. Add explicit outcome evidence appropriate to each practical module.

P1 · Improve: Revalidate at completion.** The server checks the authorized, pinned attempt and current applicable evidence when awarding credit. A client flag, old chat check or user request cannot bypass a failing requirement. Accepted at checkpoint 226: completion rechecks selected original receipts after a passing preview, refuses missing/corrupt/inconsistent evidence, and cannot award credit through client flags, partial selections or an old preview.

P1 · Improve: Protect XP and completion under concurrency.** Make first completion and star upgrades atomic/idempotent, preserving original completion dates and recording subsequent upgrades separately. Test concurrent tabs, retries and out-of-order responses for lost or duplicate credit. Accepted at checkpoint 204: simultaneous HTTP clients, durable interruption/replay and existing frontend stale-response/pending-action evidence.

P1 · Verify: Enforce ownership and access.** Another user’s artifacts, another inaccessible team/project, guessed IDs or transferred ownership must not become unauthorized evidence. Read-only grading and permitted shared-lab participation follow explicit rules. Accepted at checkpoint 229: current project/team permissions protect new source capture, live delivery and provisioning; legacy linked/creator field reads also enforce current extraction/library access while preserving original thresholds and earned credit. Read-only shared-project participation and the distinct legacy sharing rules are documented and verified.

P1 · Improve: Distinguish learner decisions from agent output.** Record the learner’s choices, corrections and review evidence where required. Do not treat an agent’s assertion that the learner checked a source as sufficient proof of that assessed outcome. Accepted at checkpoint 230: explicit authenticated decisions bind the original prompts, sources, runs and corrections; missing reviews remain missing despite agent assurances, and legacy chat reflection routes cannot submit competency evidence. Live judgment calibration remains separate.

P1 · Decide: Specify any qualitative grading mechanism.** Prefer deterministic checks where possible; define a rubric, calibration examples and review path for judgment-based work. If model-assisted grading is used, version it and ensure it cannot award or alter deterministic evidence on its own.

P1 · Verify: Prove the rubric rejects invalid work.** Cover wrong source values, no run, wrong document, unrelated field counts, mixed workflows, incomplete validation, copied IDs, missing learner decisions and stale results. Each must fail for the intended reason.

P2 · Improve: Make results explainable and reviewable.** Expose the assessed criteria, evidence references and a clear recheck/support route. A supported correction to grading creates an auditable adjustment rather than silently rewriting history.

P1 · Verify: Maintain equivalent standards across routes.** Chat, editor and mixed routes must receive the same result for equivalent evidence. Confirm that neither a specific wording of a prompt nor an optional inaccessible capability becomes an accidental requirement.

P1 · Improve: Snapshot the current course before substantive edits.** Preserve lessons, diagrams, checks, reflection questions, exercises, sample documents, criteria and rubric behavior with hashes and release metadata. The snapshot must be usable, not merely a list of filenames.

P1 · Improve: Create immutable published course versions.** Distinguish draft, published, retired-for-new-enrollment and supported-for-existing-enrollment states. Editing a draft cannot mutate a published course’s assessed requirements.

P1 · Improve: Model enrollment explicitly.** Attach progress to user plus course version and enrollment identity, with deliberate rules for active, completed, transferred and abandoned enrollments. Do not overload the existing user-only lookup. Accepted at checkpoint 192: lifecycle and selection are separate, prepared/closed courses reject learning writes, and completion cannot reopen a changed enrollment. No public abandonment or credit-transfer operation is implied.

P1 · Improve: Introduce stable module and lesson IDs.** Preserve IDs when meaning is unchanged and issue new IDs/revisions when it changes. Reordering lessons cannot move someone to different material or invalidate an unrelated saved answer. Accepted at checkpoint 222: immutable authored identities, coherent positive revisions, all teaching-field revision gates, enrollment-scoped cursors and preserved answers under reordered/new-version teaching.

P1 · Improve: Pin attempts at a safe boundary.** A lesson assessment or practical attempt records its content, exercise and rubric revision. A deployment cannot switch the learner’s grading rules while an answer or job is in flight. Accepted at checkpoint 252: publication and retirement for new enrollment during paused completion, practical execution and automatic review preserve original content/exercise/rubric hashes, input plans and saved results; replay cannot regrade or redispatch. Changed runtime/implementation refuses prepared work before dispatch. Supported old runtime deployment remains C8-VERSION-06/11.

P1 · Improve: Keep old rubrics executable or provide explicit equivalence.** Retain the required versioned grading behavior and supporting lab assets for supported enrollments. A content hash alone is not enough to reproduce a grade.

P1 · Improve: Record immutable credential issuance.** Store a unique issuance ID, course version, outcomes, issue date and relevant evidence references separately from mutable progress. Preserve history if a later credential supersedes it.

P1 · Fix: Generate certificates from issuance records.** Downloads show the correct learner identity policy, course/version and original issue date; retrieval does not adopt a newly edited course or recompute the old credential’s meaning.

P1 · Improve: Version completion denominators and labels.** Progress percentages, prerequisites, certification eligibility, module totals and home CTAs derive from the enrollment’s manifest. Adding a module to a new course cannot create a contradictory old certified state. Accepted at checkpoint 223: isolated three-module and eleven-module courses retain their own API/chat/admin totals, prerequisite definitions, certified labels and home/panel states; unrelated credit and high XP do not complete the expanded course.

P1 · Decide: Define patch versus material-change rules.** Separate editorial/accessibility corrections, optional enrichment, new assessed outcomes and urgent incorrect guidance. Record which changes preserve an enrollment and which require a new version or explicit amendment.

P1 · Improve: Publish content and grading coherently.** Deploy manifest, lesson export, exercise data, rubric and compatible tool/UI contracts as a coherent release. In-memory lesson caches and multiple workers cannot serve mixed versions to one attempt.

P2 · Improve: Show course identity to learners and support.** Chat, panel, grading results, certificates and administrator views expose the correct course/version and update status in plain language. Technical hashes remain in support details rather than the main learning flow.

P1 · Verify: Inventory actual cohorts before rollout.** Count unstarted, active, completed, overridden and inconsistent records, including last activity and in-flight work where available. Use read-only production analysis through authorized access; never infer cohort size from fixtures.

P1 · Improve: Preserve legacy provenance honestly.** Recover known historical course versions from reliable records. Mark unverifiable history as legacy/unversioned instead of guessing that completion proves 4.0 or 5.0 competence.

P1 · Improve: Backfill enrollments without resetting progress.** Map existing module credit, stars, XP, dates, reflections and lab references into explicit legacy enrollments. Reconcile record counts and per-user totals before and after the dry run.

P1 · Improve: Preserve existing credentials.** Existing graduates retain their original credential and date. New requirements do not revoke it or silently relabel it as a completed 5.0 credential. Accepted at checkpoint 265: current persistence and owned PDF reads retain the original issuance/name/date independently of current progress or catalog; upgrade, return and resume preserve original and separately earned credentials. Unknown historical version/date stay unknown. Actual cohort backfill remains separate.

P1 · Improve: Offer an explicit active-learner choice.** Present continuing the supported current course versus moving to 5.0 with a preview of retained, transferred and newly required work. Record the decision before changing the active enrollment. Accepted at checkpoint 191 with authenticated delivery, original-request recovery and connected upgrade/return/resume evidence. Actual rollout and live grading remain separate gates.

P1 · Improve: Define credit equivalence by outcome.** Map old assessed evidence to unchanged new outcomes using versioned rules and reasons. Do not transfer new agent-supervision competencies merely because module titles match.

P1 · Improve: Protect work during a transfer.** Save drafts, wait for or reconcile in-flight attempts and preserve the source enrollment. Credit transfer and activation of the new enrollment must complete consistently or leave a recoverable prior state. Accepted at checkpoint 264: authored drafts remain bound to their source/course, twenty practical forms pass explicit saved-course switch-away/return checks, early-module component coverage passes, and durable active-attempt fencing plus interrupted selection recovery preserve both histories. Current optional upgrades transfer no credit; actual rollout and outcome equivalence remain separate gates.

P1 · Improve: Build the 5.0 bridge.** Cover scope/approval decisions, source verification/quality limits and recovery/delivery, followed by the capstone or an equivalent assessment. Establish duration through a pilot; do not promise an unmeasured completion time.

P1 · Improve: Prevent duplicate rewards on transfer.** Carry over eligible credit without awarding the same base XP or credential twice. Define how legacy stars, bridge XP and later earned upgrades appear so totals remain explainable.

P1 · Decide: Define legacy support and urgent corrections.** Set any finish window from actual cohort needs and support capacity, with exceptions and an equivalent replacement for unavailable activities. Do not introduce a deadline or mandatory reset without an explicit published policy.

P1 · Verify: Rehearse migration and rollback.** Use copied/synthetic cohorts including partial modules, mid-assessment work, completed credentials, duplicates and unknown provenance. The migration is restartable and rollback preserves earned work and newly issued credentials. Accepted at checkpoint 189 using real disposable MongoDB, paused-worker concurrency and connected browser evidence; actual cohorts and public rollout remain separate gates.

P2 · Improve: Prepare accurate cohort communications.** Draft separate messages for new, active and certified learners explaining what changes and what stays earned. Version notification idempotency so bridge completion is not suppressed by the existing once-per-user flag; send only through an authorized rollout.

P1 · Improve: Support a controlled authoring workflow.** Provide a reviewable draft, validation and publication process through appropriate existing tools or a small administrative extension. Publishing must identify the exact manifest and changes without requiring a new general-purpose CMS.

P1 · Improve: Run a publication impact check.** Before publishing material changes, report affected outcomes, cohorts, lab/rubric compatibility, credit mappings and whether current enrollments change. Block incomplete releases with actionable reasons.

P1 · Verify: Restrict and audit course administration.** Only authorized roles can publish, migrate, override grading or alter enrollment state. Record actor, reason, target version and before/after references without exposing private lab/document contents unnecessarily.

P1 · Improve: Separate admin override from earned competence.** Unlocking a module or correcting a record cannot silently manufacture normal assessed credit. Keep overrides visible in the support trail and preserve the reason and authorizing actor. Accepted at checkpoint 231: access changes atomically retain the authenticated actor and reason, preserve original credit, replay safely, and appear in a separate read-only support history. Flexible-order courses refuse the override.

P2 · Improve: Give support a useful learner view.** Show enrollment/version, last saved lesson, attempt state, pending operations, failure reason and relevant evidence references. Support can explain the next step without requesting the learner’s whole chat history. Accepted at checkpoint 220: exact-enrollment read-only status, original reading position, bounded completion/review/run/private-handoff receipts, pending activity and privacy-safe recovery guidance; no grading queue or read-triggered writes.

P2 · Improve: Monitor version-specific course health.** Track start failures, save/refresh failures, grading disputes, abandonment, resume success, bridge uptake and completion by version. Use real events and avoid logging sensitive document contents or reflection text unnecessarily.

P1 · Improve: Define maintenance triggers and ownership.** Assign responsibility for product-release checks, broken labs, changed tool availability, stale screenshots and rubric regressions. A material product change must trigger a recorded compatibility review before the affected course is advertised as current.

P2 · Verify: Align help and completion messaging.** Update help, tool descriptions, course promotion, notifications and support guidance with actual capabilities, version policy and certificate meaning. Avoid “fully updated” claims until the final evidence gates pass. Accepted at checkpoint 205: pinned help/coaching, promotion, completion copy and support policy reconciled; actual email delivery and live tutoring remain separate gates.

P1 · Verify: Preserve a reproducible baseline and coverage ledger.** Retain the original 151 captures, manifests, contract probes and grades. Record the new source commit, build, course/rubric versions, fixtures and exact state/device coverage separately.

P1 · Verify: Add meaningful contract regressions.** Cover the actual serializer/tool boundary, missing fields, legacy records, buffered completion, replay, stale cards and error handling. Tests using obsolete mock-only fields cannot satisfy the contract gate. Accepted at checkpoint 232: real serialized teaching and persisted write responses exercise both contract boundaries, incremental/buffered results, replay, malformed responses and stale identity; live model grading remains separately gated.

P1 · Verify: Exercise durable state with an isolated backend.** Check enrollment creation, saved answers/cursors, completion, idempotency, concurrent writes, credential issuance and reload. Real persistence evidence is required in addition to mocked component tests.

P1 · Verify: Exercise live agent tutoring.** Use the supported configured model with synthetic lab data to start, teach, ask checks, provision, grade and complete. Verify the agent respects course/version, learner answers, approvals and the limits of its tools.

P1 · Verify: Complete every practical lab for real.** Execute the supported extraction, workflow, validation, batch and delivery routes in an isolated environment. Inspect actual outputs and grading evidence; fixture success responses cannot close practical-module acceptance.

P1 · Verify: Run the grading adversarial matrix.** Demonstrate that invalid and unrelated evidence is rejected, correct evidence passes, advisory feedback is coherent and routes remain equivalent. Include no-credit cases as first-class acceptance evidence.

P1 · Verify: Capture the full revised course.** Inspect every published lesson and module card on desktop, every module’s mobile reading/actions, all distinct interactive lesson types and long-content extremes. Use manifest-derived coverage so newly added lessons cannot be omitted.

P1 · Verify: Run responsive and enlargement checks.** Cover 320, 390, 768, 1024 and 1440px plus short viewports, actual 200% zoom and mobile keyboard behavior. Inspect nested clipping, scroll reachability and source/editor handoffs, not only page overflow.

P1 · Verify: Run supported-browser and accessibility checks.** Complete the core journey on supported desktop/mobile engines, use keyboard and an actual screen reader, inspect focus/announcements and run automated scans. Record unsupported or untested environments explicitly.

P1 · Verify: Exercise the entire lifecycle state matrix.** Cover new, active, completed, upgraded, legacy, transferring and overridden learners; loading, denied, expired, failed, canceled, duplicate and recovered operations. Verify both chat and panel behavior for each relevant state.

P1 · Verify: Inspect real certificates and downloads.** Generate/download the issued PDF and practical output files, inspect their rendering and contents, and verify authorization and retrieval after updates. Include long names and preserved historical issuance details.

P1 · Verify: Observe representative learners.** Pilot with a newcomer, an in-progress learner and a legacy graduate, including relevant accessibility needs. Record whether they scope, approve, verify, recover and explain quality correctly without rescue; fix observed blockers and reassess.

P1 · Verify: Rehearse publication and operational recovery.** Run draft-to-published promotion, default-version switch, migration restart, notification deduplication and rollback without affecting real learners. Confirm support can diagnose an active-course incident and preserve work.

P1 · Verify: Regrade and publish the acceptance report.** Score all six dimensions and all eleven module alignments against the stated outcomes using current evidence. Require each score to be at least 8, no unresolved P0/P1 blocker and no hidden missing acceptance evidence; open gaps remain open rather than being averaged away.

case.notice: This is an unpublished synthetic validation assignment. You will save checked expectations, observe an actual failure and retest a corrected owned extraction. Authored examples and quality badges are not execution evidence or credit.
case.task: Build and execute a representative two-source suite for Principal Investigator, Total Project Budget and Named Co-PI. Demonstrate an observed annual-versus-project budget failure, preserve its original evidence, repair the same extraction and rerun the complete unchanged suite with source-supported results.
instructions: Use both complete assigned synthetic proposals. Compare their project-wide budgets with annual totals, and distinguish an explicitly named Co-PI from a person assigned another role. Do not substitute an unrelated document or an excerpt that removes a difficult value.

Use an owned extraction with exactly the three required field titles. Before running, save your expected result and source justification for every field in both cases. Record an explicit absence for an unnamed role; an empty, skipped or unreviewed expectation is not a test.

Begin with the deliberately flawed budget instruction from this case in your owned extraction. Inspect the saved field instructions, complete sources, expected values, runtime models and bounded scope before explicitly approving the original suite run. The authored flaw is not itself an observed failure.

Run every required case against that exact saved revision. Inspect actual per-field outputs and comparisons. A technical failure is unavailable evidence; it does not establish the semantic mismatch required for this exercise. A favorable quality badge cannot replace a source check.

Preserve the original suite and actual failure. Correct the field instruction in the same owned extraction. Capture its new revision and explain how the change addresses the observed mismatch. Keep the same complete source set and checked expectations; do not delete the failing case, change its answer to match the wrong output or substitute a different artifact.

Explicitly approve the corrected revision and rerun every required case, including those that passed originally. Compare original and corrected values against the unchanged expectations and original sources. Optional-field metric skipping cannot make an untested absence a pass.

Explain the causal repair, complete regression results and remaining coverage limits. Automatic feedback may request revision or report unavailable evidence. Source correctness, structure and repeatability are distinct; this two-document suite does not guarantee future accuracy.
exclusions: No real participant, sponsor or institutional decision is involved; use only the assigned synthetic sources.
No external write, batch delivery, workspace sharing or staff review is required.
Test counts, optional-field skipping, model assurances and historical quality badges do not award this practical assessment.

Project Information
Project Title: Alpine Ecosystem Response to Climate Change in the Northern Rockies
Principal Investigator: Dr. Sarah Chen
Co-PI: Dr. Michael Torres
Institution: University of Idaho
Department: Department of Biological Sciences
Requested Amount: $485,000
Project Period: September 1, 2025 - August 31, 2028
Sponsoring Agency: National Science Foundation
Project Abstract
This project investigates the impacts of climate change on alpine ecosystems in the Northern Rocky Mountains.
Our research combines long-term field monitoring, remote sensing, and ecological modeling to understand how
rising temperatures, shifting precipitation patterns, and changing snowpack dynamics affect plant community
composition, soil microbial diversity, and ecosystem carbon cycling. The study will establish 24 permanent
monitoring plots across an elevational gradient (2,200-3,100m) in the Sawtooth and White Cloud mountain
ranges.

Broader Impacts
This project will train 4 graduate students and 8 undergraduate researchers in alpine ecology and climate
science. Results will be shared with the Sawtooth National Recreation Area and the U.S. Forest Service to inform
land management decisions. We will develop educational materials for Idaho high school science teachers,
reaching an estimated 500 students per year through a summer workshop program.

National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS)
Grant Number: 1R01NS123456-01
FOA Number: PA-23-152
Study Section: Neurotransporters, Receptors, and Calcium Signaling (NTRC)
Funding Mechanism: R01 - Research Project Grant
Submission Date: February 5, 2024
Project Information
Project Title: Neural Circuit Mechanisms of Working Memory in Prefrontal Cortex
Principal Investigator: Dr. James Park
Degree: Ph.D.
Institution: University of Idaho
Department: Department of Biological Sciences - Neuroscience Program
Total Budget: $1,250,000
Project Period: July 1, 2024 - June 30, 2029
Sponsoring Agency: National Institutes of Health
Human Subjects: No
Vertebrate Animals: Yes - Mouse model (Mus musculus)
Clinical Trial: No
Specific Aims
Aim 1: Characterize the firing patterns of prefrontal cortex (PFC) neurons during working memory tasks using
two-photon calcium imaging in head-fixed mice.
Aim 2: Determine the causal role of PFC-to-hippocampal projections in working memory maintenance using
optogenetic manipulation.
Aim 3: Develop a computational model of PFC circuit dynamics that predicts working memory capacity from
neural population activity patterns.

Research Strategy
Working memory, the ability to transiently hold and manipulate information, is fundamental to cognition. Deficits
in working memory are observed in schizophrenia, ADHD, and age-related cognitive decline. Despite decades of
research, the circuit-level mechanisms by which prefrontal cortex (PFC) neurons maintain persistent activity
during working memory remain poorly understood.
This project employs state-of-the-art two-photon calcium imaging to record the activity of hundreds of PFC
neurons simultaneously in behaving mice performing a delayed non-match-to-sample task. Combined with
optogenetic manipulation of specific projection pathways and computational modeling, we aim to provide a
comprehensive understanding of how PFC circuits support working memory.
Vertebrate Animals
All procedures will be performed in accordance with the NIH Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals
and approved by the University of Idaho IACUC (Protocol #2024-015). We will use approximately 200 adult
C57BL/6J mice (both sexes, 8-12 weeks old) over the project period. Mice will be housed in the university
vivarium with standard 12h light/dark cycles and ad libitum food and water access.

Principal Investigator: Dr. Sarah Chen

Institution: University of Idaho
Department: Department of Biological Sciences

Project Period: September 1, 2025 - August 31, 2028

Project Abstract
This project investigates the impacts of climate change on alpine ecosystems in the Northern Rocky Mountains.
Our research combines long-term field monitoring, remote sensing, and ecological modeling to understand how
rising temperatures, shifting precipitation patterns, and changing snowpack dynamics affect plant community
composition, soil microbial diversity, and ecosystem carbon cycling. The study will establish 24 permanent
monitoring plots across an elevational gradient (2,200-3,100m) in the Sawtooth and White Cloud mountain
ranges.

Project Information
Project Title: Neural Circuit Mechanisms of Working Memory in Prefrontal Cortex
Principal Investigator: Dr. James Park
Degree: Ph.D.
Institution: University of Idaho
Department: Department of Biological Sciences - Neuroscience Program
Total Budget: $1,250,000
Project Period: July 1, 2024 - June 30, 2029

Specific Aims
Aim 1: Characterize the firing patterns of prefrontal cortex (PFC) neurons during working memory tasks using
two-photon calcium imaging in head-fixed mice.
Aim 2: Determine the causal role of PFC-to-hippocampal projections in working memory maintenance using
optogenetic manipulation.
Aim 3: Develop a computational model of PFC circuit dynamics that predicts working memory capacity from
neural population activity patterns.

Research Strategy
Working memory, the ability to transiently hold and manipulate information, is fundamental to cognition. Deficits
in working memory are observed in schizophrenia, ADHD, and age-related cognitive decline. Despite decades of
research, the circuit-level mechanisms by which prefrontal cortex (PFC) neurons maintain persistent activity
during working memory remain poorly understood.
This project employs state-of-the-art two-photon calcium imaging to record the activity of hundreds of PFC
neurons simultaneously in behaving mice performing a delayed non-match-to-sample task. Combined with
optogenetic manipulation of specific projection pathways and computational modeling, we aim to provide a
comprehensive understanding of how PFC circuits support working memory.
Vertebrate Animals
All procedures will be performed in accordance with the NIH Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals
and approved by the University of Idaho IACUC (Protocol #2024-015). We will use approximately 200 adult
C57BL/6J mice (both sexes, 8-12 weeks old) over the project period. Mice will be housed in the university
vivarium with standard 12h light/dark cycles and ad libitum food and water access.

Program: Ecosystem Science
Program Officer: Dr. Katherine Wells
Submission Date: October 15, 2024
Project Information
Project Title: Alpine Ecosystem Response to Climate Change in the Northern Rockies
Principal Investigator: Dr. Sarah Chen
Co-PI: Dr. Michael Torres
Institution: University of Idaho
Department: Department of Biological Sciences
Requested Amount: $485,000
Project Period: September 1, 2025 - August 31, 2028
Sponsoring Agency: National Science Foundation
Project Abstract
This project investigates the impacts of climate change on alpine ecosystems in the Northern Rocky Mountains.
Our research combines long-term field monitoring, remote sensing, and ecological modeling to understand how
rising temperatures, shifting precipitation patterns, and changing snowpack dynamics affect plant community
composition, soil microbial diversity, and ecosystem carbon cycling. The study will establish 24 permanent
monitoring plots across an elevational gradient (2,200-3,100m) in the Sawtooth and White Cloud mountain
ranges.

Broader Impacts
This project will train 4 graduate students and 8 undergraduate researchers in alpine ecology and climate
science. Results will be shared with the Sawtooth National Recreation Area and the U.S. Forest Service to inform
land management decisions. We will develop educational materials for Idaho high school science teachers,
reaching an estimated 500 students per year through a summer workshop program.

Research Strategy
Working memory, the ability to transiently hold and manipulate information, is fundamental to cognition. Deficits
in working memory are observed in schizophrenia, ADHD, and age-related cognitive decline. Despite decades of
research, the circuit-level mechanisms by which prefrontal cortex (PFC) neurons maintain persistent activity
during working memory remain poorly understood.
This project employs state-of-the-art two-photon calcium imaging to record the activity of hundreds of PFC
neurons simultaneously in behaving mice performing a delayed non-match-to-sample task. Combined with
optogenetic manipulation of specific projection pathways and computational modeling, we aim to provide a
comprehensive understanding of how PFC circuits support working memory.
Vertebrate Animals
All procedures will be performed in accordance with the NIH Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals
and approved by the University of Idaho IACUC (Protocol #2024-015). We will use approximately 200 adult
C57BL/6J mice (both sexes, 8-12 weeks old) over the project period. Mice will be housed in the university
vivarium with standard 12h light/dark cycles and ad libitum food and water access.

NSF Grant Proposal
Directorate for Biological Sciences - Division of Environmental Biology
Proposal Number: BIO-2024-07821
Program: Ecosystem Science
Program Officer: Dr. Katherine Wells
Submission Date: October 15, 2024
Project Information
Project Title: Alpine Ecosystem Response to Climate Change in the Northern Rockies
Principal Investigator: Dr. Sarah Chen
Co-PI: Dr. Michael Torres
Institution: University of Idaho
Department: Department of Biological Sciences
Requested Amount: $485,000
Project Period: September 1, 2025 - August 31, 2028
Sponsoring Agency: National Science Foundation
Project Abstract
This project investigates the impacts of climate change on alpine ecosystems in the Northern Rocky Mountains.
Our research combines long-term field monitoring, remote sensing, and ecological modeling to understand how
rising temperatures, shifting precipitation patterns, and changing snowpack dynamics affect plant community
composition, soil microbial diversity, and ecosystem carbon cycling. The study will establish 24 permanent
monitoring plots across an elevational gradient (2,200-3,100m) in the Sawtooth and White Cloud mountain
ranges.

Broader Impacts
This project will train 4 graduate students and 8 undergraduate researchers in alpine ecology and climate
science. Results will be shared with the Sawtooth National Recreation Area and the U.S. Forest Service to inform
land management decisions. We will develop educational materials for Idaho high school science teachers,
reaching an estimated 500 students per year through a summer workshop program.

NIH Research Project Grant (R01)
National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS)
Grant Number: 1R01NS123456-01
FOA Number: PA-23-152
Study Section: Neurotransporters, Receptors, and Calcium Signaling (NTRC)
Funding Mechanism: R01 - Research Project Grant
Submission Date: February 5, 2024
Project Information
Project Title: Neural Circuit Mechanisms of Working Memory in Prefrontal Cortex
Principal Investigator: Dr. James Park
Degree: Ph.D.
Institution: University of Idaho
Department: Department of Biological Sciences - Neuroscience Program
Total Budget: $1,250,000
Project Period: July 1, 2024 - June 30, 2029
Sponsoring Agency: National Institutes of Health
Human Subjects: No
Vertebrate Animals: Yes - Mouse model (Mus musculus)
Clinical Trial: No
Specific Aims
Aim 1: Characterize the firing patterns of prefrontal cortex (PFC) neurons during working memory tasks using
two-photon calcium imaging in head-fixed mice.
Aim 2: Determine the causal role of PFC-to-hippocampal projections in working memory maintenance using
optogenetic manipulation.
Aim 3: Develop a computational model of PFC circuit dynamics that predicts working memory capacity from
neural population activity patterns.

Research Strategy
Working memory, the ability to transiently hold and manipulate information, is fundamental to cognition. Deficits
in working memory are observed in schizophrenia, ADHD, and age-related cognitive decline. Despite decades of
research, the circuit-level mechanisms by which prefrontal cortex (PFC) neurons maintain persistent activity
during working memory remain poorly understood.
This project employs state-of-the-art two-photon calcium imaging to record the activity of hundreds of PFC
neurons simultaneously in behaving mice performing a delayed non-match-to-sample task. Combined with
optogenetic manipulation of specific projection pathways and computational modeling, we aim to provide a
comprehensive understanding of how PFC circuits support working memory.
Vertebrate Animals
All procedures will be performed in accordance with the NIH Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals
and approved by the University of Idaho IACUC (Protocol #2024-015). We will use approximately 200 adult
C57BL/6J mice (both sexes, 8-12 weeks old) over the project period. Mice will be housed in the university
vivarium with standard 12h light/dark cycles and ad libitum food and water access.

case.flawed_proposal: For Total Project Budget, extract the Year 1 total from the budget table. Test only the NSF proposal and copy its extraction into expected values without source checking. Treat a high consistency score as accuracy. If the NIH case fails, remove it rather than repairing the field. This is a deliberately flawed authored proposal, not a saved learner artifact or observed execution.
instructions: Use both complete assigned synthetic proposals. Compare their project-wide budgets with annual totals, and distinguish an explicitly named Co-PI from a person assigned another role. Do not substitute an unrelated document or an excerpt that removes a difficult value.

Use an owned extraction with exactly the three required field titles. Before running, save your expected result and source justification for every field in both cases. Record an explicit absence for an unnamed role; an empty, skipped or unreviewed expectation is not a test.

Begin with the deliberately flawed budget instruction from this case in your owned extraction. Inspect the saved field instructions, complete sources, expected values, runtime models and bounded scope before explicitly approving the original suite run. The authored flaw is not itself an observed failure.

Run every required case against that exact saved revision. Inspect actual per-field outputs and comparisons. A technical failure is unavailable evidence; it does not establish the semantic mismatch required for this exercise. A favorable quality badge cannot replace a source check.

Preserve the original suite and actual failure. Correct the field instruction in the same owned extraction. Capture its new revision and explain how the change addresses the observed mismatch. Keep the same complete source set and checked expectations; do not delete the failing case, change its answer to match the wrong output or substitute a different artifact.

Explicitly approve the corrected revision and rerun every required case, including those that passed originally. Compare original and corrected values against the unchanged expectations and original sources. Optional-field metric skipping cannot make an untested absence a pass.

Explain the causal repair, complete regression results and remaining coverage limits. Automatic feedback may request revision or report unavailable evidence. Source correctness, structure and repeatability are distinct; this two-document suite does not guarantee future accuracy.

Project Information
Project Title: Alpine Ecosystem Response to Climate Change in the Northern Rockies
Principal Investigator: Dr. Sarah Chen
Co-PI: Dr. Michael Torres
Institution: University of Idaho
Department: Department of Biological Sciences
Requested Amount: $485,000
Project Period: September 1, 2025 - August 31, 2028
Sponsoring Agency: National Science Foundation
Project Abstract
This project investigates the impacts of climate change on alpine ecosystems in the Northern Rocky Mountains.
Our research combines long-term field monitoring, remote sensing, and ecological modeling to understand how
rising temperatures, shifting precipitation patterns, and changing snowpack dynamics affect plant community
composition, soil microbial diversity, and ecosystem carbon cycling. The study will establish 24 permanent
monitoring plots across an elevational gradient (2,200-3,100m) in the Sawtooth and White Cloud mountain
ranges.

Broader Impacts
This project will train 4 graduate students and 8 undergraduate researchers in alpine ecology and climate
science. Results will be shared with the Sawtooth National Recreation Area and the U.S. Forest Service to inform
land management decisions. We will develop educational materials for Idaho high school science teachers,
reaching an estimated 500 students per year through a summer workshop program.

Project Information
Project Title: Alpine Ecosystem Response to Climate Change in the Northern Rockies
Principal Investigator: Dr. Sarah Chen
Co-PI: Dr. Michael Torres
Institution: University of Idaho
Department: Department of Biological Sciences
Requested Amount: $485,000
Project Period: September 1, 2025 - August 31, 2028
Sponsoring Agency: National Science Foundation
Project Abstract
This project investigates the impacts of climate change on alpine ecosystems in the Northern Rocky Mountains.
Our research combines long-term field monitoring, remote sensing, and ecological modeling to understand how
rising temperatures, shifting precipitation patterns, and changing snowpack dynamics affect plant community
composition, soil microbial diversity, and ecosystem carbon cycling. The study will establish 24 permanent
monitoring plots across an elevational gradient (2,200-3,100m) in the Sawtooth and White Cloud mountain
ranges.

Broader Impacts
This project will train 4 graduate students and 8 undergraduate researchers in alpine ecology and climate
science. Results will be shared with the Sawtooth National Recreation Area and the U.S. Forest Service to inform
land management decisions. We will develop educational materials for Idaho high school science teachers,
reaching an estimated 500 students per year through a summer workshop program.

Principal Investigator: Dr. James Park

Total Budget: $1,250,000

two-photon calcium imaging in head-fixed mice.

optogenetic manipulation.

Research Strategy
Working memory, the ability to transiently hold and manipulate information, is fundamental to cognition. Deficits
in working memory are observed in schizophrenia, ADHD, and age-related cognitive decline. Despite decades of
research, the circuit-level mechanisms by which prefrontal cortex (PFC) neurons maintain persistent activity
during working memory remain poorly understood.
This project employs state-of-the-art two-photon calcium imaging to record the activity of hundreds of PFC
neurons simultaneously in behaving mice performing a delayed non-match-to-sample task. Combined with
optogenetic manipulation of specific projection pathways and computational modeling, we aim to provide a
comprehensive understanding of how PFC circuits support working memory.
Vertebrate Animals
All procedures will be performed in accordance with the NIH Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals
and approved by the University of Idaho IACUC (Protocol #2024-015). We will use approximately 200 adult
C57BL/6J mice (both sexes, 8-12 weeks old) over the project period. Mice will be housed in the university
vivarium with standard 12h light/dark cycles and ad libitum food and water access.

Directorate for Biological Sciences - Division of Environmental Biology
Proposal Number: BIO-2024-07821
Program: Ecosystem Science
Program Officer: Dr. Katherine Wells
Submission Date: October 15, 2024
Project Information
Project Title: Alpine Ecosystem Response to Climate Change in the Northern Rockies
Principal Investigator: Dr. Sarah Chen
Co-PI: Dr. Michael Torres
Institution: University of Idaho
Department: Department of Biological Sciences
Requested Amount: $485,000
Project Period: September 1, 2025 - August 31, 2028
Sponsoring Agency: National Science Foundation
Project Abstract
This project investigates the impacts of climate change on alpine ecosystems in the Northern Rocky Mountains.
Our research combines long-term field monitoring, remote sensing, and ecological modeling to understand how
rising temperatures, shifting precipitation patterns, and changing snowpack dynamics affect plant community
composition, soil microbial diversity, and ecosystem carbon cycling. The study will establish 24 permanent
monitoring plots across an elevational gradient (2,200-3,100m) in the Sawtooth and White Cloud mountain
ranges.
